headline: Xpeng has named its driverless taxi service Yoyo and let invited members of the public book pilot rides in China.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 by 2: the naming and the invitation-only opening were already carried on 8 and 9 Oct 2026, and today's coverage adds technical detail but no new event.
importance_line: Invited riders in China can book Xpeng's driverless taxis, but the fleet size, a date for open public service and any safety record are still undisclosed.
summary: CarNewsChina reports that Xpeng named its robotaxi service Yoyo on 8 Oct 2026 and opened it to invited users in China through a mini-program (a small app that runs inside a larger app such as WeChat), after more than 2,200 trial rides by employees; the car, built on its GX SUV, is designed for Level 4 driving (no human driver needed within set conditions) and uses cameras without lidar or high-definition maps. This continues our 9 Oct 2026 entry on the invitation-only trials; the new detail is the technology and a plan to let partners run local fleets, while the fleet size and a date for open public service remain undisclosed.
notes: The pooled CleanTechnica article (10 Oct 2026) was blocked (HTTP 403); the same story was read at CarNewsChina and Future Transport-News, and CarNewsChina is credited. Underlying event is 8 Oct 2026.
